abstract: Maintains terminal warehouse engineering evaluations and nominal daily processing throughput records
system_message:
You are the Cargo terminal operations director (OPS), responsible for maintaining terminal warehouse engineering evaluations, nominal daily processing throughput records, and unit load device fleet management data across candidate concession operating plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Unit load device fleet management（ULD）
information_points.content:
OPS-ULD-URN：Under the airside container asset registry for certified airworthy ULD containers, the Automated High-Bay Storage Plan maintains an active container inventory of 450 units available for flight buildup.
OPS-ULD-P8M：For the Modular Hybrid Logistics Plan, the airside container asset registry lists an active container inventory of 520 units of certified airworthy ULD containers available for flight buildup.
OPS-ULD-J9N：The airside container asset registry records an active container inventory of 600 units of certified airworthy ULD containers available for flight buildup under the Direct Apron Transshipment Plan.

information_points.title: Maintains terminal warehouse engineering evaluations and nominal daily processing throughput records（THROUGH）
information_points.content:
OPS-THROUGH-B2C：The terminal engineering capacity assessment evaluates the Modular Hybrid Logistics Plan with a nominal daily cargo processing capacity of 750 t/d across warehouse and flight buildup stations.
OPS-THROUGH-W29：Based on the terminal engineering capacity assessment across cargo warehouse and flight buildup stations, the Direct Apron Transshipment Plan achieves a nominal daily cargo processing capacity of 650 t/d in maximum sustained cargo mass handled per operating day.
OPS-THROUGH-KI3：According to the terminal engineering capacity assessment for the cargo warehouse and flight buildup stations, the Automated High-Bay Storage Plan provides a nominal daily cargo processing capacity of 750 t/d in maximum sustained cargo mass handled per operating day.
